expired_token.title: That QR code expired
expired_token.body: Pairing codes work once and expire after 5 minutes. Show a new code and scan it again.

lost_connection.title: Connection lost
lost_connection.body: Your phone stopped responding. Check that its screen is on, the browser tab is open and both devices are on the same Wi-Fi.

ice_failed.title: Video connection failed
ice_failed.body: Your phone and computer could not reach each other directly. They may be on different networks, or a firewall is blocking OpenCamera.

negotiation_failed.title: Couldn't start the video stream
negotiation_failed.body: The phone's browser and OpenCamera couldn't agree on a video format. Try Safari on iPhone or Chrome on Android.

no_network.title: No local network
no_network.body: This computer isn't connected to a local network. Connect to the same Wi-Fi as your phone.

port_in_use.title: Port already in use
port_in_use.body: Another app is using OpenCamera's network port. Choose a different port in Settings.

server_failed.title: Couldn't start the connection service
server_failed.body: OpenCamera couldn't listen for phones on your network. Check your network settings or restart the app.

unknown.title: Something went wrong
unknown.body: OpenCamera ran into an unexpected problem. Details are available in About › Diagnostics.

certificate.intro: It says “Your connection is not private” or “This Connection Is Not Private”. That's expected here.
certificate.iphone: iPhone Safari: tap Show Details › visit this website

reasons.https: Phone browsers only allow camera access on secure (https) pages.
reasons.authority: Public certificate authorities can't issue certificates for private addresses like 192.168.x.x, so OpenCamera creates its own certificate on this computer.
reasons.encrypted: The connection is still encrypted and stays on your local network.
reasons.remembered: Browsers usually remember your choice, so you'll normally see this once per phone. It comes back if this computer's network address changes, since OpenCamera then makes a new certificate, or if the phone's browser data is cleared.

device.title: Device
device.suspended: Paused while the phone screen is off
device.saverActive: Battery saver limits video to {{fps}} fps because the phone is low on battery or running hot.

pair.title: Connect a device
pair.description: Scan this code with your phone's camera. Your phone and computer must be on the same Wi-Fi network.
pair.scanBody: Open your phone's camera and tap the link that appears.
pair.startBody: Allow camera access when asked. The code works once.
pair.hint: Phone can't open the page? Check it's on the same Wi-Fi as this computer ({{address}}). Guest networks often block devices from seeing each other, and your firewall must allow OpenCamera on private networks.

performance.title: Performance
performance.scaled: Auto bitrate shrank the picture by {{scale}}× to keep up with the network.

presets.title: Presets
presets.empty: Save the current phone and computer settings to switch between setups in one click.
presets.needsPhone: Connect a phone to save a preset.

preview.reconnectingBody: Keep the OpenCamera page open on your phone. It reconnects automatically.
preview.noPhoneBody: Scan a QR code with your phone to use its camera as a webcam. No app install needed.
preview.background: Phone browser is in the background
preview.backgroundBody: Your phone's operating system pauses the camera while the browser isn't visible. Bring the OpenCamera page back to the front.
preview.pausedBody: Resume video from the phone or the Camera page.

streamWarning.tip: Lower the resolution or frame rate on the Camera page, or tap the moon button on the phone to dim its screen.

hot.title: Phone is running hot
hot.body: Hot phones slow down, which makes video choppy. {{tip}}

cpu.title: Phone can't keep up
cpu.body: Its processor is overloaded, often because it's warm. {{tip}}

bandwidth.title: Wi-Fi is limiting quality
bandwidth.body: Move the phone closer to the Wi-Fi router, or lower the resolution on the Camera page.

update.title: Updates
update.label: Software update
update.idle: Check whether a newer version of OpenCamera is available.
update.downloading: Downloading… The app restarts when done.
update.downloadingPercent: Downloading {{percent}}%… The app restarts when done.

virtualCamera.title: Virtual camera
virtualCamera.bannerSetup: Install the virtual camera to finish setup
virtualCamera.bannerBody: Video apps can't see OpenCamera until it is installed.
virtualCamera.activeHint: Select OpenCamera Virtual Camera as the camera in Zoom, Teams, Discord, OBS or your browser.

dashboard.description: Your phone's camera, available to every app on this computer.

camera.description: Phone settings apply immediately. Computer settings apply when you click Save changes.
camera.needsPhone: Connect a phone to change these settings.
camera.lensBody: Lenses your phone's browser makes available.
camera.resolutionBody: Only sizes your phone's camera supports can be chosen.
camera.qualityBody: Low latency keeps motion smooth, high quality keeps detail when Wi-Fi is busy.
camera.bitrateBody: Auto adapts picture size to your Wi-Fi, Manual caps video data at a fixed rate.
camera.batterySaverBody: Drops to 15 fps when the phone's battery is at 20% or less, or when it runs hot.
camera.cameraOnBody: Turning it off releases the phone's camera and the virtual camera shows the placeholder.
camera.framingBody: Fit shows the whole picture with bars, Fill crops to 16:9.
camera.outputSizeBody: Picture size apps receive. Higher sizes use more CPU, and your phone's resolution still limits the detail.
camera.placeholderBody: What apps see while the phone is disconnected or paused.
camera.gridBody: Rule-of-thirds guide in the preview only.

settings.description: Changes are applied when you click Save changes.
settings.launchAtLoginBody: Start OpenCamera when you sign in to this computer.
settings.keepRunningBody: Closing the window hides OpenCamera in the system tray so phones stay connected. Quit from the tray menu.
settings.autoReconnectBody: At startup, listen on your local network so paired phones reconnect without a new QR code. Phones not seen for 24 hours must scan again. Takes effect next launch.
settings.notificationsBody: Notify when a phone connects or the connection is lost while OpenCamera is in the background.
settings.setupGuideBody: Walk through installing the virtual camera and connecting a phone again.
settings.statusBody: Phones connect to this address. Nothing is reachable from outside your local network.
settings.addressBody: Choose the adapter your phone's Wi-Fi network is on if the QR code doesn't open.
settings.portBody: TCP port for the phone page and signaling (1024-65535).
settings.iceServerBody: Optional. Only needed if your phone and computer can't connect directly, e.g. on isolated networks.
settings.developerModeBody: Records detailed connection, video and decoder logs, and shows them live under Diagnostics on the About page. Never includes pairing codes or device secrets.

about.description: Turns your phone into a wireless webcam. Video goes directly from your phone's browser to this computer over your local network. There are no accounts, no analytics and no cloud servers, and nothing is recorded.
about.resetBody: Restores every setting. Paired phones are kept.
about.diagnosticsBody: Safe to share: contains no pairing codes, device secrets or video.
about.diagnosticsLive: Developer mode is on, so detailed lines appear live.

welcome.title: Turn your phone into a webcam
welcome.body: Two quick steps. No app, no account. Works in Zoom, Teams, OBS and more.
welcome.cameraBody: Adds OpenCamera Virtual Camera to Zoom, Teams, Discord, OBS and your browser.
welcome.readyBody: Pick it as your camera in any video app.
welcome.permissionWindows: Windows will ask for permission. Click Yes.
welcome.permissionPassword: You'll be asked for your password.
welcome.phoneBody: Phone and computer on the same Wi-Fi.
welcome.scanBody: Open your phone's camera, point it at the code and tap the link.
welcome.warningBody: Your browser will say the page isn't private. That's expected.
welcome.allowBody: Tap Allow when asked. Your video then shows up here.
welcome.expectedBody: OpenCamera runs on your own network with its own certificate, so phone browsers flag it. The video stays encrypted.

connected.title: Phone connected
connected.body: {{name}} is streaming to OpenCamera Virtual Camera.

batteryLow.title: Phone battery low
batteryLow.body: Plug in your phone to keep streaming.
